description: Width tiers for Design and Technologies Foundation (ACARA v9). One entry per descriptor.
subject: Design and Technologies

generation_rules.notes: AC9TDEFK01 uses phenomena_contexts (concept/understanding descriptor). AC9TDEFP01 uses task_contexts (process/capability descriptor). First Nations elaborations present in AC9TDEFK01.

width_notes.minimum: The narrowest context or task that honestly satisfies the descriptor's command term. Every student in the class meets this floor before the class moves on.
width_notes.typical: Full descriptor scope as ACARA intended — grounded in the most common elaboration cases. Reflects sound standard practice for the band.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add phenomena or task contexts, not difficulty. Each item is a concrete direction for advancing students. First Nations elaborations included as default wider directions where ACARA provides them.

AC9TDEFK01.minimum_width: Identify at least two familiar products or environments and state that people designed and made them; identify one design decision and explain its purpose.
AC9TDEFK01.typical_width: Explore products, services and environments across home, school and community contexts; identify design decisions in each and explain how they serve a purpose; ask questions about why things were designed the way they were.
wider: Identify how First Nations Australians have long designed and produced domestic items — explore how the Lamalama Peoples weave bags using fibres from two different plants; discuss what the item was designed for and how choices reflect purpose
Explore how a local playground has shade structures and accessible design features — identify specific design decisions and explain why they were made
Ask questions about the design of products from the local store — why was the packaging chosen? how do the text and images attract attention? connect specific design decisions to their purpose
elaborations: identifying how First Nations Australians have long designed and produced domestic items including clothing, tools and shelter, for example the Lamalama Peoples of the eastern Cape York Peninsula weave the reddish coloured fibres from Acacia latifolia alternately with white coloured fibres from Brachychiton diversifolium to produce a striped woven bag

exploring how local delivery services meet different needs of people, for example describing how gift packages can be sent to and from people who live in different locations and how online shopping items arrive at a person's home
exploring how an environment such as a local playground may have shade structures to protect users and be designed to allow access for all
describing how community gardens, public swimming pools and parks are designed to help people stay healthy

asking questions about the design of products from the local store, for example why certain packaging materials might have been selected, and how people design the text and images on the packaging to attract people's attention

AC9TDEFP01.minimum_width: Identify a purpose; generate one design idea; use materials and equipment to make a solution; share one opinion about what was made.
AC9TDEFP01.typical_width: Generate and communicate design ideas through drawing or modelling across multiple design contexts; use materials, components and equipment safely to make solutions; evaluate using personal preferences; connect evaluation back to the original purpose.
wider: Identify a real school-environment purpose (e.g. sand blowing from sandpit, birds getting into bins, accessibility at school) — generate ideas, choose one and make it; evaluate whether it addresses the purpose
Design and make bee hotels to attract native bees to the school garden — generate multiple ideas, choose one, make it using available materials, evaluate against the purpose
Make a ramp or obstacle game using re-used or found materials — test the solution and explain what worked and what could be improved
Record evaluation of a made solution using audio or video — describe strengths, weaknesses and what to change next time
elaborations: identifying a purpose for designing and making a solution, for example the sand keeps blowing out of the sandpit, the birds keep flying into the waste bin and taking food scraps or people with disability need to know where they can park at school

exploring ideas by drawing or modelling and choosing the most suitable idea, for example drawing or modelling designs for bee hotels to attract native bees to the school garden and choosing one to make, and changing perspectives from front view to plan view
evaluating what they have made using personal preferences, for example using a smiley face Likert scale
exploring how available materials can be used or re-used in construction play, for example using blocks and rain gutters or cardboard to make a ramp to roll a ball or toy car down

practising a range of technical skills safely using equipment, for example joining techniques when making a product from materials, such as a greenhouse to keep a seedling warm or a trellis for holding up tomato plants
assembling components of systems and checking they function as planned, for example making and testing a bowling, stacking or obstacle game with discarded food containers or packaging
